questions.question: In Class 8 of a school, the ratio of students playing cricket to those playing football is 27 ∶ 13, while the ratio of those playing football to those playing hockey is 26 ∶ 14. If the total number of students in Class 8 is 470, and each student plays exactly one game, find the percentage of students of the class playing cricket. [Give your answer correct to two decimal places.]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of students playing cricket to those playing football is 27 : 13 and

Ratio of students playing football to those playing hockey is 26 : 14.

Total no. of students is 470

**Calculations:**

Ratio of students playing cricket, football and hockey respectively is 27 × 26 : 26 × 13 : 13 × 14 

⇒ 702 : 338: 182

⇒ 351: 169 : 91

⇒ 27 : 13 : 7

Now, according to the question, 

(27 + 13 + 7)k = 470

⇒ 47 × k = 470

⇒ k = 10

Now , no. of students playing cricket = 27k = 27 × 10 = 270

Percentage required = 270/470 × 100 = 57.45%** **

**∴ The percentage reduired = 57.45%**

⇒ 127-39

⇒ 88

**∴ The single equivalent discount is 88%.**

questions.question: In a company, there are only two types of employees, workers, and officers. 35% of the employees are officers and the average monthly salary of an officer is ₹39,000 more than the combined average monthly salary of all employees. What is the difference between the average monthly salaries of an officer and a worker?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Officers : Workers = 35% : 65% = 7 : 13.

Deviation of Officer's salary from the combined average = +₹39,000.

Applying the net deviation rule: Sum of deviations = 0.

7 × (+39,000) + 13 × (Worker's deviation) = 0.

Worker's deviation = −(7 × 39,000) ÷ 13 = −₹21,000.

Total difference = Officer's surplus + Worker's deficit = 39,000 + 21,000 = ₹60,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹60,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage of Officers = 35%

Percentage of Workers = 100% − 35% = 65%

AvgOffᵢ꜀ₑᵣ − AvgTₒₜₐₗ = ₹39,000

**Formula Used:**

Weighted Average: n₁(A₁ − Aₐvg) = n₂(Aₐvg − A₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b23348bb97cdfe1aec5cfe9df57aa3fcdf32bd14c9c4f6d7e68f19b91bb7b8ac.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Ratio of Officers (nO) to Workers (nW) = 35 : 65 = 7 : 13

⇒ Let AvgTₒₜₐₗ be A, then AvgOffᵢ꜀ₑᵣ = A + 39,000

⇒ Let AvgWₒᵣₖₑᵣ be AW

⇒ 7 × (AvgOffᵢ꜀ₑᵣ − A) = 13 × (A − AvgWₒᵣₖₑᵣ)

⇒ 7 × (39,000) = 13 × (A − AvgWₒᵣₖₑᵣ)

⇒ A − AvgWₒᵣₖₑᵣ = (7 × 39,000) ÷ 13

⇒ A − AvgWₒᵣₖₑᵣ = 7 × 3,000 = 21,000

⇒ Difference = AvgOffᵢ꜀ₑᵣ − AvgWₒᵣₖₑᵣ

⇒ Difference = (AvgOffᵢ꜀ₑᵣ − A) + (A − AvgWₒᵣₖₑᵣ)

⇒ Difference = 39,000 + 21,000 = 60,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹60,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alligation Rule for Averages

The ratio of the quantities of two groups is the inverse ratio of the differences of their individual averages from the combined average: n₁/n₂ = (A₂ − Aₐvg) / (Aₐvg − A₁).

Net Deviation Method

In any distribution, the sum of the products of the frequency and the deviation of each value from the mean is always zero: ∑ fᵢ(xᵢ − x̄) = 0.

Weighted Average Formula

The combined average of two groups is given by Aₐvg = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) / (n₁ + n₂), where n represents the number of items and A represents the average.

questions.question: In a Panchayat election, three candidates were there in the fray. The losing candidates got an equal number of votes and the winning candidate got as many votes as the rest of the two got collectively. If the total votes polled were 1500, find the number of votes that the winning candidate got, assume all votes polled were valid.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Winner got the votes equal to the sum of rest two candidates

Rest candidates got equal amount of votes .

**Calculations:**

Let the loosing candidates got x votes each 

Then, winner got 2x votes.

Now, according to question, 

2x + x + x = 1500

⇒ x = 375

⇒ Winner got 2x = 2 × 375

**∴ Winner got 2x = 750 votes.**

questions.question: On dividing 8675123 by a certain number, the quotient is 33611 and the remainder is 3485. The divisor is ______.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number = 8675123

Quotient = 33611

Remainder = 3485

**Concept Used:**

Number = Quotient × Divisor + Remainder

**Calculations:**

⇒ 8675123 = 33611 × Divisor + 3485

⇒ 8675123 – 3485 = 33611 × Divisor

⇒ 8671638 = 33611 × Divisor

⇒ Divisor = (8671638)/(33611)

⇒ Divisor = 258

**∴ The required value of the Divisor is 258.**

questions.question: RA and RB are two tangents from a common point ‘R’ outside the circle with centre ‘O’, having a radius of 6 cm. If ∠ARB = 70°, find the measure of the angle AOB.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius = 6 cm 

∠ARB = 70°

**Concept Used:**

Sum of the angles of a quadrilateral is 360°

The angle between the radius and the tangent of a circle is 90°

**Calculation:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/10ad6bb1d49d4fe270d3670c70f4d782d20f026a7bd6de419bce1ecbd8bccc13.png] **

⇒ The 4 points A, B, R and O make a quadrilateral

⇒ ∠RAO = ∠RBO = 90°

⇒ ∠RAO + ∠AOB + ∠RBO + ∠ARB = 360°

⇒ 90° + ∠AOB + 90° + 70° = 360°

⇒ ∠AOB = 360° – 250° = 110°

**∴ The value of ∠AOB is 110°.**

questions.question: The time taken by a 180 m long train running at a speed of 54 km/h to cross a man standing on the platform is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of train = 180 m

Speed of train = 54 km/h

**Concept Used:**

Speed = (Distance)/(Time)

**Calculation:**

Firstly, we will change the value of speed from km/h to m/s.

⇒ 54 km/h = 54times (5)/(18)

⇒ 54 km/h = 15 m/s

Putting the value in the speed formula, we get

⇒ 15 m/s = (180)/(Time)

⇒ Time = (180)/(15)

⇒ Time = 12 seconds

**∴ The time taken by the train to cross a man standing on the platform is 12 seconds.**

questions.question: If 49 litres of a milk solution has 63% milk in it, then how much milk should be added to make the concentration of milk 70% in the solution?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equating the constant quantity of water before and after adding milk:

Initial Water % × Initial Volume = Final Water % × Final Volume

⇒ 37% × 49 = 30% × Final Volume

⇒ Final Volume = (37 × 49) ÷ 30 = 1813 ÷ 30 L

⇒ Added Milk = Final Volume − Initial Volume = (1813 ÷ 30) − 49 = 343 ÷ 30 = 11 ¹³/₃₀ litres

**∴ The correct answer is 11 ¹³/₃₀ litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total volume of initial mixture = 49 litres

Milk concentration in initial mixture = 63%

Desired milk concentration in final mixture = 70%

Concentration of pure milk added = 100%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/49b68d247ebe9a0f2e81a11e747f873037ac07891b24a6e0135a4d85f3d00d7a.png] 

**Calculations:**

Using the rule of alligation, the ratio in which the initial mixture and pure milk must be mixed is:

⇒ Ratio = (100 − 70) : (70 − 63)

⇒ Ratio = 30 : 7

We are given that 30 units of the initial mixture corresponds to 49 litres.

⇒ 30 units = 49 L

⇒ 1 unit = 49 ÷ 30 L

⇒ Pure milk to be added (7 units) = 7 × (49 ÷ 30) = 343 ÷ 30 L

⇒ Quantity of milk added = 11 ¹³/₃₀ litres

**∴ The correct answer is 11 ¹³/₃₀ litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation

It is a visual mathematical method used to find the ratio in which two ingredients at their respective concentrations must be mixed to produce a mixture of a desired average concentration. The ratio is determined by cross-subtracting the target value from the components.

Constant Quantity Method

When only one component (e.g., milk) is added or removed from a mixture, the absolute quantity of the other component (e.g., water) remains strictly unchanged. Equating the initial and final volumes of this unchanged part yields the new total volume directly.

Replacement Formula

When a specific volume of a mixture is repeatedly replaced by one of its pure components, the remaining amount of the original un-added component is calculated as: Final Amount = Initial Amount × (1 − Replaced Volume ÷ Total Volume)ⁿ.
